metadata.body:
Populate gRPC client `server.address` and `server.port` from configured channel targets rather than channel authority alone.

Library users can supply the target explicitly on all supported gRPC versions, without depending on gRPC's internal target-aware interception API:

```java
GrpcTelemetry telemetry = GrpcTelemetry.create(openTelemetry);
String target = "dns:///orders.example.com:8443";
ManagedChannelBuilder<?> channelBuilder = ManagedChannelBuilder.forTarget(target);
channelBuilder.intercept(telemetry.createClientInterceptor(target));
```

The no-argument `createClientInterceptor()` continues to use channel authority. For custom name resolvers, use an explicit `scheme://...` target.

For automatic capture, use this experimental API instead of registering the interceptor directly:

```java
Experimental.addClientInterceptor(telemetry, channelBuilder);
```

`Experimental` is in `io.opentelemetry.instrumentation.grpc.v1_6.internal`. Automatic capture depends on gRPC's internal API on 1.64.0 and newer, falling back to authority on older versions or unsupported builders. The Java agent uses this automatic path.

Remove `GrpcRequest.getLogicalHost()` and `getLogicalPort()` for 3.0. Use `getServerAddress()` and `getServerPort()` instead. `getServerPort()` returns `null` rather than `-1` when the port is unavailable.
